But if {EMPLOYER} wanted Coyle's Reckoning destroyed rather than merely moved, the band sails off whole to become someone else's problem, and maybe yours again down the road.

costs.resource: The band's punishment, traded away for the station and the hostages intact.
costs.risk: A band let go is a band that raids again, maybe back here, certainly somewhere.

options.title: Take the Bunkers First
advantages: Before the main assault, slip a small team into the fuel tanks and hold them. Take away the band's scuttle card before it can play it.
With the fuel tanks secured, you can pressure the band freely without risking the station.
Removes the worst outcome entirely: no scuttle can destroy the station.
disadvantages: A team in the fuel tanks sits in the most deadly compartment on the station, where one stray round is a disaster.
Peeling off a fuel-tank team weakens your main effort against the core.
If the band reaches the tanks first or in force, your team is fighting in the one place a firefight cannot be allowed.
options.consequence: You reach for the band's last card before the band can. Securing the fuel tanks turns the scuttle threat into an empty bluff and frees up every other choice. The price is a team sent into the deadliest room on the station, where success is silence and failure is a fireball that needs no rig at all.

costs.resource: A detachment sent to hold the fuel tanks, the station's most dangerous compartment, through the whole main fight.
costs.risk: Any firefight in the fuel tanks ends the station, whether the band rigged them or not.

entries.event: Your approach plays out: a paying ship at the dock, a bait convoy sprung, or an assault on the spine. Coyle's Reckoning realizes it is dealing with a hunter, not a customer, and the toll watch goes to battle stations.
The band pulls in toward the core habitat ring and the hostages. That is the instinct of a band whose leverage is people, not ground.

The band decides whether to scuttle. If it reads the station as lost, the leader sends crew to the fuel tanks and the scuttle clock starts. If the band still thinks it can win or make a deal, the tanks stay clean.
The fight reaches the core. The hostages' compartment is now inside the battle, so every choice from here is made with civilians and the station's controls in the line of fire.
The situation resolves: the station is taken intact, taken rigged, or breaking apart. A band not beaten or bought off by now has either scuttled or made a last stand in the core around the operators.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: There is no fixed clock on this one. The deadline is the band's own judgment. It arrives the moment Coyle's Reckoning decides the station is lost and reaches for the fuel tanks. Take the station, buy the band out, or seize the fuel tanks before that moment comes, and the region keeps both its only recharge point and its operators. Push the band past that point with nowhere to go, and the prize the contract exists to save dies with the people held inside it. That means a kilometer of irreplaceable truss and {HOSTAGE_COUNT} hostages, lost because a hunter pressed a cornered enemy one compartment too far.

opforSketch.composition: Coyle's Reckoning, a raider band turned tollkeepers: roughly a reinforced company afloat — {BAND_CREW} crew (Regular boarders, Veteran core around the leader), shipboard and anti-boarding weapons, plus 3-4 light salvage 'Mechs and gun-cutters that can deploy onto the docking spine and outer truss but not safely inside the fragile core. The band's real weapon is the hostages and the scuttle threat, not its firepower. Generator should keep interior fighting infantry-scale, allow 'Mech and vehicle engagement only on the spine and truss, and treat the fuel bunkers and core as no-fire ground where the contract is won or lost.
opforSketch.behavior: Coyle's Reckoning fights like men who have a hostage in one hand and a match in the other: confident while they hold the leverage, quick to consolidate around the core when pressed, and willing to threaten the unthinkable to keep what they have taken. They run a businesslike toll and would rather be paid than fight. But cornered with no exit, the leader will reach for the bunkers — not from fanaticism, but because a band that has made this many enemies knows surrender is its own death sentence, and would rather bargain from the edge of a fireball than from a cell.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN ROAD
forks.trigger: The station is taken intact and working, the operators are alive, and the fuel tanks were never rigged.
forks.consequence: The recharge station reopens under honest management. {EMPLOYER}'s shipping firms offer you the standing contract every merc outfit wants: garrison the station, take a cut of an honest toll, and hold the region's only chokepoint against the next band that eyes it. That next band may even be the survivors of this one.

forks.name: OPERATION DARK LIGHTHOUSE
forks.trigger: The station is scuttled or crippled, or the operators are killed.
forks.consequence: The region loses its only recharge point, and you lose the whole purpose of the contract. {EMPLOYER}'s follow-up job is salvage and rescue: get clear whatever the band left of the station and its people. This stretch of the frontier now faces a week on solar for every JumpShip that passes. It is a harder, poorer region, and you helped make it that way.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND RECKONING
forks.trigger: The station is saved, but Coyle's Reckoning gets away intact, through the door or by fighting its way out.
forks.consequence: The toll is ended here, but the band is loose out there: humiliated, robbed of its prize, and carrying a grudge and your name. {EMPLOYER} funds the chase. Run Coyle's Reckoning down before it seizes another chokepoint. This time you have the station's rescued operators, who can tell you exactly how the band thinks.

storyElementSeed: In the station core, a civilian operator still keeps the recharge logs up to date, out of forty years of habit. She enters each ship the band tolls in the same neat hand she has always used. The work is the one thing the men with guns have not taken from her. And a log, she knows, is a kind of message to whoever finally comes.

resourceGates.lackingText: No owned hull to play the fat merchant: the disguise runs on a chartered freighter whose real crew must be kept clear of the boarding team — add 12,000 C-bills and a captain who now knows the unit boards stations for a living.

Insufficient funds to assemble a convincing bait convoy: the lure shrinks to a single ship the band may not bother massing for — weaken the draw, and accept the core garrison stays heavier than the plan needs.

title: OPERATION DROWNED ROAD
skeleton: a counter-guerrilla force hired to break a pirate-supplied insurgency must realize the fight is not the insurgents but their hidden resupply artery, a flooded-mine smuggling route that arms them, and must find and sever that underwater conduit while every sweep against the fighters themselves only recruits more, so the decisive ground is a drowned tunnel nobody knew was a road
inspiration: the Malayan Emergency — defeating an insurgency by cutting its supply chain rather than chasing its fighters
situation:
{EMPLOYER} has been losing a small war on {WORLD} for a year. It has finally admitted it cannot win the way it has been fighting. The trouble is {WORLD}'s flooded {DISTRICT} mine country. Picture a sprawl of worked-out pit mines, half of them filled with water, laced with drowned tunnels and pumping channels. That country has bred an insurgency {EMPLOYER}'s garrison cannot put down. Every sweep through the mine villages kills a few fighters and makes a dozen more. Every reprisal turns a sullen population into one that hides the guerrillas out of anger. Trust the failure part of this: a year of garrison after-action reports all say the same thing. Why it is failing is a rough guess, but the loss itself is plain.

Here is what {EMPLOYER}'s garrison missed, and what {EMPLOYER} has hired your unit through {NPC:employer-contact} to fix. It comes down to supply. These insurgents are too well armed to be simple farmers with rifles. They have salvaged autocannon rounds, reloaded SRMs, medical stores, and the everyday gear a fighting force burns through. Something is feeding them on a schedule, and it is coming from off {WORLD}. {NPC:intel-source} is now fairly sure the supply line runs through the flooded mines. The theory is that a pirate band uses the drowned tunnels as a hidden road. They move arms in under the water, where no patrol looks, and surface them inside villages no sweep can seal. Chase the fighters and the insurgency grows. Cut the road that arms it and it starves.

The hard terrain is the flooded workings. That means kilometers of pit lakes, sunken tunnels, and pumping channels. You can patrol the surface, but the real traffic moves below it. A 'Mech can wade the shallows and hold the causeways between pits. The supply road, if it is real, runs through drowned tunnels a 'Mech cannot enter and a patrol boat cannot map. To find the road you must work out which flooded tunnel the band keeps pumped and open. The only real proof is being on it when a shipment moves.

Two clocks are running: the population's patience and {EMPLOYER}'s money. Your unit has {CAMPAIGN_DAYS} days of contract. Push too hard with sweeps to flush the road's surface signs and you recruit for the enemy, just as the garrison did. Move too slowly with quiet intelligence work and the insurgency stays armed while {EMPLOYER}'s bills pile up. Your job is to find a hidden road through drowned country without fighting the war that hid it.

objectives.primary: Break the insurgency by cutting off its supply. Find the smuggling road through the flooded mines and shut it for good, so the fighters run out of the arms and gear that keep them fighting.
objectives.secondary: Do it without recruiting for the enemy. No reprisals, no leveled villages, nothing that pushes {WORLD}'s sullen population to join the insurgency.
objectives.bonus: Find and stop the pirate band that runs the road, not just the road itself. Take out the crew so {WORLD}'s insurgency cannot reopen the route after your unit leaves.

complications.name: Every Sweep Recruits
complications.text: The garrison lost this war by fighting it. Each sweep through the mine villages killed fighters and created more. The people's anger is the insurgency's recruiting tool, and rough tactics keep it working.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Harsh actions against villages or civilians roll against an insurgent-recruitment track. As that track rises, it replaces every guerrilla you kill and then some. It also drains the local intelligence you need to find the road. Holding back is not weakness here. It is the only way to win.

complications.name: The Road Below the Water
complications.text: The road runs through drowned tunnels no 'Mech can enter and no surface patrol can see. You can control the surface of the mine country. The real traffic moves where you cannot follow.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You do not know where the road is, and force on the surface alone will not find it. To learn which flooded tunnel is the live road, you need intelligence work, diver scouting, or catching a shipment in transit. 'Mech sweeps will not do it, because the road simply runs beneath them.

complications.name: The Schedule Nobody Shares
complications.text: Shipments move on the band's clock, not yours, and the insurgents who take them surface in a different village each time. Catching one shipment is not the same as cutting the road. The band has backup tunnels and the patience to wait you out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The smuggling route has backups. Catching one shipment or closing one tunnel does not break the road unless you have mapped its single choke point. Act too early on a partial picture and you close one branch while teaching the band to use the others.

decisionPoints.name: How to Find the Road
decisionPoints.context: The road is real, hidden, and built with backups, and the war that hid it punishes the wrong kind of searching. You must decide how to hunt for a road through drowned country without fighting the people who live over it.

options.title: Win the Villages
advantages: Turn the people's anger around. Protection, fair dealing, and real help to the mine villages buys the intelligence the garrison's reprisals destroyed
Villagers who feel safe will name the tunnels the band uses. You find the road from the surface, from people who watched it get built
Lowers the recruitment track and cuts off the insurgency's shelter at the same time
disadvantages: Winning trust is slow. It takes weeks of steady presence against a {CAMPAIGN_DAYS}-day clock while the insurgency stays armed
The band's own people live in the villages, so you court the population under the insurgents' eyes
If your generosity looks like weakness, it may embolden the fighters before it cuts them off
options.consequence: You fight the war the garrison should have fought: for the people, not against them. Do it with patience and the villages hand you both the road and the insurgency's shelter. Do it too slowly and the contract runs out while you make friends and the fighters stay supplied.

costs.resource: 30 days of steady presence and real aid to the mine villages, while the insurgency stays armed the whole time
costs.risk: if you court the villages too slowly, the contract runs out before you find the road

options.title: Map It by Stealth
advantages: Send specialist divers and hidden sensors into the flooded tunnels to map the network yourself. You find the road without involving the population at all
It is technical, deniable, and safe from the recruitment problem
A mapped network shows you the one choke point the whole road depends on
disadvantages: Diving worked-out flooded mines is deadly work. It needs special gear and moves slowly through kilometers of drowned tunnel
The band may guard or booby-trap its tunnels. A diver spotted means a shipment warned and a route changed
Sensors in the water tell you where the road is, not when it runs
options.consequence: You read the drowned road on your own terms, one instrument and one lungful at a time. A clean mapping job hands you the choke point with no village ever the wiser. A diver lost or spotted in the dark tunnels warns the band and ruins the map you were building.

costs.resource: specialist divers and sensor gear committed to deadly, slow work in flooded tunnels
costs.risk: a spotted diver warns the band, which reroutes the road you nearly had

options.title: Bait a Shipment
advantages: Feed the band a fake order. Send a phony insurgent request for a big, specific resupply and force a large shipment onto the road where you are waiting
Catches the road in use, proving both the route and the schedule at once
Lets you pick the time and place of the intercept
disadvantages: Faking insurgent traffic means breaking into the insurgency's own communications. That is hard, and getting caught burns your source
Bait a shipment and miss it and you teach the band the route is watched, while handing the insurgents real arms you failed to stop
The intercept happens underwater or at a surfacing point, the ground you control least
options.consequence: You reach into the enemy's own supply order and pull the road to the surface. A clean bait puts a shipment right where you can take it and proves the whole road. A blown one arms the insurgency, warns the band, and tells everyone the outsiders are playing the supply game.

costs.resource: a break-in on insurgent communications that burns the moment the bait is seen as fake
costs.risk: a baited shipment that slips through arms the enemy and warns the road in one stroke

decisionPoints.name: How to Cut It
decisionPoints.context: The road is mapped and its choke point is found: the one drowned tunnel or pumping station the whole road depends on. You decide how to cut it, knowing the band has backups and the people have long memories.

options.title: Collapse the Chokepoint
advantages: Bring down the key tunnel or wreck the pumping station that keeps the road open. This is a lasting physical cut the band cannot reopen fast
It is decisive. A flooded, collapsed tunnel takes months of work to replace
It ends the resupply cleanly, without a shot fired at a villager
disadvantages: Collapsing worked mines risks the flooding and cave-ins the villages live among. A careless blast is the very reprisal you were trying to avoid
A physical cut alone leaves the band intact to dig a new road
Your map found one choke point, but it may have missed a second the band kept in reserve
options.consequence: You drown the road for good and trust the band cannot rebuild before the contract ends. A clean collapse starves the insurgency as its arms run dry. A collapse that floods a village undoes a month of goodwill in an afternoon and hands the insurgency its anger back.

costs.resource: demolition in worked mine country, where a bad blast floods the people you needed on your side
costs.risk: a physical cut leaves the road-builders free to dig another road

options.title: Ambush the Conduit
advantages: Hold the choke point and take the next shipment whole: the arms, the smugglers, and proof of the pirate band behind the road
Catches the road-builders, not just the road. This is your path to the bonus objective
A shipment seized and a smuggling crew captured is intelligence on the whole network
disadvantages: An ambush at the choke point is a fight on the band's chosen ground, underwater or at a surfacing point
Taking one shipment does not collapse the road. The band reroutes once it learns the choke point is blown
A firefight near a village is the recruitment risk at its loudest
options.consequence: You spring the trap on the road itself and take everything that moves on it. A clean ambush nets the smugglers, the arms, and the thread back to the band. It also warns the road that its choke point is known. Now it is a race: you exploit what you caught while the band reroutes what it has left.

costs.resource: a fight on the band's chosen underwater ground, with a village close enough to hear it
costs.risk: an ambush sprung is a choke point blown, so the band reroutes the road you just proved

options.title: Turn the Conduit
advantages: Don't cut the road, own it. Take the choke point quietly and feed the insurgency tampered supplies: dud ammunition, tracked shipments, and broken trust
Breaks the insurgency from inside its own supply line, with no sweep and no collapse
Tracked shipments map every cell the road feeds, and dud arms wreck the fighters' faith in their own supply
disadvantages: Running a captured smuggling road means holding the choke point in secret for weeks, unseen by band and insurgents alike
If you are found out, the whole thing becomes a double disaster: the band warned, the insurgents enraged, and your deception exposed
This is the most complex option, with the most ways to fall apart
options.consequence: You become the road you set out to cut, feeding the insurgency its own defeat one tampered shipment at a time. Kept secret, it unravels the insurgency from the inside, because fighters who cannot trust their ammunition stop fighting. Discovered, it is the worst outcome here: an exposed trick that arms and enrages everyone at once.

costs.resource: secret control of the choke point for weeks, with the whole plan riding on never being found by either enemy
costs.risk: a turned road discovered arms the insurgents, warns the band, and exposes your unit all at once

entries.event: Trigger. A shipment moves, a diver is spotted, or a sweep turns up a sign. The road goes active and the band's smuggling crew is on it with arms aboard.
First signs of a surfacing. Insurgent pickup cells move toward a surfacing point in one of the mine villages, pulling you toward a populated area.
The insurgent screen goes up. Local fighters move to cover the surfacing: a few squads of guerrillas who know the ground, fighting to protect the supply, not to win.
If you do not intercept, the shipment surfaces and scatters into the village. After this the arms are handed out and the road's traffic is hidden again until the next run.
The band's smuggling crew pulls back down the tunnels. If you have not cut or caught the road by now, it has run another shipment and the insurgency is resupplied for another cycle.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Each shipment cycle is its own short clock. Once the arms surface and scatter into a village by T+4:00, they are gone into the insurgency, and the road goes dark until the band runs it again. The campaign clock is {CAMPAIGN_DAYS} days of contract. The real deadline is the one the garrison already missed: find and cut the road before the hunt for it recruits a new generation of fighters. Fight the fighters and the clock beats you the way it beat the garrison. Cut the road and the insurgency starves on your schedule instead of growing on its own.

opforSketch.composition: Two linked enemies. The insurgency: {INSURGENT_STRENGTH} local fighters in cells, lightly armed but for what the conduit brings (Green individually, Veteran on their home mine-ground), plus a handful of armed IndustrialMech conversions and technicals hidden in the workings. The smuggling band: a pirate crew running the drowned road — divers, small submersibles, a surface mother-ship offshore, and a light salvage 'Mech section guarding surfacing points (Regular). Generator should keep the insurgent fight infantry-and-conversion scale on causeways and in villages, reserve the band's heavier elements for surfacing-point clashes, and treat the flooded galleries as ground no 'Mech enters.
opforSketch.behavior: The insurgents fight like a supplied population: hit-and-fade on home ground, sheltering in villages, growing with every reprisal and shrinking only when their supply dries up. They protect shipments fiercely because the arms are their lifeline. The smuggling band is commercial and cautious — it runs the road for profit, guards it only enough to keep it working, and reroutes or abandons a blown gallery rather than fight for it, because the road is the asset and a road can always be dug somewhere else.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY POWDER
forks.trigger: The conduit is permanently cut, the insurgency is starved, and the population was not turned against the unit.
forks.consequence: The insurgency withers as its arms run out. {EMPLOYER} keeps your unit on to garrison the recovered mine country through the peace that follows. It is a season holding ground that no longer shoots at you, watching the flooded tunnels in case the band tries to dig a new road back in.

forks.name: OPERATION RISING WATER
forks.trigger: The conduit survives, or the unit's methods recruit the insurgency a new generation.
forks.consequence: You have repeated the garrison's defeat with better gear. The insurgency is still armed and now larger, the population is more hostile, and the pirate road still runs. If {EMPLOYER} still trusts you, its next contract is a harder and costlier version of the war you just lost.

forks.name: OPERATION SLACK TIDE
forks.trigger: The road is cut but the pirate band escapes to dig elsewhere.
forks.consequence: {WORLD}'s insurgency starves, but the band that armed it lifts off intact, taking its drowned-road know-how to the next pirate-supplied uprising. {EMPLOYER}, or its neighbors, pay for the chase: run the road-builders down before they sell the same trick to another insurgency.

storyElementSeed: A diver surfaces in a flooded tunnel lit only by her own lamp. She treads water in the black and finds what she came for, without wanting to. A guide-rope runs off into the dark in both directions, pulled tight and clearly looked after. It is somebody's road: kept up, in use, and until this second known only to them.

resourceGates.lackingText: No budget for a full dive-and-sensor effort: the mapping runs on hired local divers with sport kit and no redundancy — add 12 days, accept gaps in the map, and accept that an under-equipped diver lost in a flooded gallery is a death and a warning both.

No secure forward base to run a captured chokepoint from: the operation works out of a leased village structure under constant risk of discovery — add 8,000 C-bills and a far higher chance the deception is blown by a neighbor who notices the wrong people coming and going.

title: OPERATION DRY DOCK
skeleton: a sabotage element must permanently wreck the single dry dock that lets a raider band keep its heavy ships spaceworthy by collapsing the dock's caisson gate, where the dock is the irreplaceable thing and the demolition must read as a structural accident so the band wastes a season rebuilding rather than relocating or hunting, so the crux is the disguised one-shot denial of a fixed industrial asset under guard
inspiration: the St Nazaire Raid (Operation Chariot) — denying the enemy the only dry dock that could service its capital ships, 1942
situation:
A raider band is only as strong as its ships are spaceworthy. The band that calls itself the Hable Combine has one thing that lifts it above a local nuisance: a working dry dock. On {WORLD}'s {DISTRICT} coast sits a pre-Blackout graving dock. It is a basin you can float a DropShip into, seal off, pump dry, and then work on the hull from all sides. The Combine took the port and the dock two years ago. That dock is why its Mule-class and its two armed DropShips still fly, while every other band in the region grounds ships it can no longer maintain. Port-watch reports and a salvaged dock schematic back this up. That intelligence is 20 to 45 days old, so the picture of the band is only fairly reliable, but the dock itself is confirmed.

{EMPLOYER}, through {NPC:employer-contact}, does not want the port and does not want a pitched battle with the Combine. {EMPLOYER} wants the dock gone. The point is to make the Combine's ships start falling out of the sky as their maintenance lapses, which is what happens to hard-used hulls with nowhere to dock. And {EMPLOYER} wants it done so the Combine never knows it was attacked. A dry dock that fails as an accident buys time. If the caisson gate collapses and the basin floods and will not pump, the Combine spends a season trying to fix what it thinks broke. If it knows it was sabotaged, it spends that season relocating, retaliating, or hunting your unit instead. A wreck that looks like sabotage starts a war. A wreck that looks like a structural failure starts a salvage estimate.

The hard part is the caisson gate. That is the floating dam that seals the dock mouth against the sea. It is the dock's one weak point and also its one irreplaceable part, because no Dark Age yard can rebuild a Star League-era structure like it. Drop the caisson at the wrong moment and the basin floods out of control. With the gate down, the dock cannot be used, and if it cannot be rebuilt, that is forever. So the gate is the target, the prize, and the disguise all at once. You must wreck it in a way that looks like the gate failing on its own.

The dock is also guarded and worked. The Combine keeps a security detail on the port and a yard crew on the dock, and a hull may be in the basin under repair at any time. {NPC:intel-source} reports that the Combine's armed Mule is docked now for a drive overhaul. That report is 11 days old and only fairly reliable, but it means the basin is occupied and the yard is busy. So the window where a caisson 'failure' would do the most damage is also the window with the most witnesses.

objectives.primary: Wreck the caisson gate so the dry dock cannot be pumped or used. This permanently denies the Hable Combine its dock and grounds its heavy ships over the coming season as their maintenance lapses.
objectives.secondary: Make the wreck look like a structural accident, not sabotage. Leave no clear evidence of an attack, so the Combine repairs the dock instead of relocating, retaliating, or hunting your unit.
objectives.bonus: Catch a Combine hull in the basin when the caisson goes. A ship trapped or damaged in the flooding dock is a second irreplaceable asset denied, and it grounds the Combine even harder.

complications.name: The Irreplaceable Gate
complications.text: The caisson is the dock's one weak point, and no Dark Age yard can rebuild it. That is exactly why you must destroy it. Wrecking it costs the Combine a whole season of grief.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The caisson gate is the only objective that matters. Wrecking other dock infrastructure is repairable and fails the primary. To destroy the caisson, you must place charges at its structural weak points. Brute force will not do it, so this is a job for demolition and engineering, not 'Mech guns.

complications.name: It Must Look Like an Accident
complications.text: If the Combine sees the dock was bombed, it knows it was attacked, so it relocates and hunts you. If the dock simply fails, the Combine repairs it in place, blind to the hand that broke it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The operation carries a disguise track. Overt force, obvious charges, or a firefight at the gate turn the wreck from an accident into clear sabotage. That triggers the retaliation and relocation outcomes on the campaign layer, even if the dock is destroyed. Clean, deniable demolition keeps your season of grace.

complications.name: The Occupied Basin
complications.text: The Combine's armed Mule is in the dock for an overhaul, the yard crew is working, and the security detail is alert. The best moment to drop the caisson is also the moment the dock is most full of people who will see it drop.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The dock is guarded and worked, with a hull in the basin. Timing the caisson failure to catch the Mule earns the bonus, but it raises the witness count and the chance of detection. An empty-dock window is safer, but it gives up the trapped-ship prize.

decisionPoints.name: How to Reach the Gate
decisionPoints.context: The caisson sits at the seaward mouth of a guarded, working dock. You must get demolition charges onto a structure surrounded by the Combine's people. And you must do it without starting the fight that would unmask the whole operation.

options.title: Infiltrate by Sea
advantages: Approach the caisson from the water, using divers or a small craft in the dark. Place charges on the gate's submerged structure, where no guard walks.
This is the most deniable approach. Nothing on the landward side is disturbed, and underwater charges look like structural failure.
It bypasses the security detail and yard crew completely.
disadvantages: A sea approach to a guarded port is slow and depends on the weather. It is deadly if the swimmers are caught in the water.
Placing charges on the caisson's underside in a working basin means working just meters below the hull and crew above.
A diver found at the gate makes the sabotage plain.
options.consequence: You come for the gate the way the sea itself would, from below and unseen. A clean placement drops the caisson as a structural failure that no one can pin on an attacker. But a swimmer caught in the dark basin hands the Combine a saboteur and proof it was attacked.

costs.resource: a sea infiltration of a guarded port, dependent on the weather and unforgiving if a swimmer is found
costs.risk: a diver found at the caisson turns the whole operation from an accident into an act of war

options.title: Walk In as Yard Workers
advantages: Forged credentials get a team inside the dock as hired hands. The Dark Age's chronic shortage of skilled yard labor makes the cover easy, and it gives inside access to the caisson machinery.
The team can rig the gate's own control and ballast systems to 'fail'. That is the most convincing accident of all.
The team has time on site to place charges precisely and pick the moment.
disadvantages: A team inside the yard works among the Combine's own crew, one wrong answer from exposure.
The caisson's machinery spaces may be the most closely watched part of the dock.
If caught, the team is deep inside a hostile port with no infiltration line to retreat down.
options.consequence: You walk in the front gate wearing the enemy's coveralls and break the dock from the inside, where an accident is easiest to stage. If the cover holds, the Combine's own engineers will blame the caisson failure on metal fatigue. If it is blown, you are in a fight at the heart of the yard, and the disguise is gone with the first shout.

costs.resource: forged yard credentials and a team placed among the Combine's own crew, with one chance to pass
costs.risk: exposure inside the yard means a firefight in the worst place, and the accident disguise is lost with the first alarm

options.title: Stage a Diversion Raid
advantages: Mount an obvious nuisance raid elsewhere on the port, such as a cargo grab or a fuel-depot hit. It pulls the security detail away from the dock while a small team works the caisson.
It gives the demolition team room and time at the gate.
The diversion can be a real, deniable pirate-style raid that explains itself.
disadvantages: A raid anywhere on the port puts the Combine on alert, and an alert dock is a watched dock, even if the watch is looking the wrong way.
Running two operations at once doubles the coordination risk and the chance one of them goes loud near the gate.
A diversion that is too obviously a diversion makes the Combine wonder what it was meant to miss, and look at the dock.
options.consequence: You buy the gate team its window by giving the Combine something louder to look at. A well-pitched diversion pulls attention off the dock, and the caisson fails while the Combine chases shadows. A clumsy one alerts the whole port and invites the Combine to connect the noise to the gate.

costs.resource: a second force committed to a diversionary raid, plus the alert it raises across the whole port
costs.risk: a diversion that smells like a diversion makes the Combine guard the very thing it was meant to ignore

decisionPoints.name: When to Drop the Caisson
decisionPoints.context: The charges are placed. You choose the moment the gate fails. That choice trades the trapped-ship prize against the witness count and the cleanness of the disguise.

options.title: When the Mule Is in the Basin
advantages: Drop the caisson with the Combine's armed Mule in the dock. Flood the basin and you deny a dry dock and a heavy hull in one stroke.
This is the deepest possible blow to the Combine's spacelift.
A ship damaged in a flooding dock is plausibly an accident victim itself.
disadvantages: With a hull in it under overhaul, the basin is at its most crewed and most watched.
The trapped ship's crew are witnesses with every reason to investigate why the dock 'failed' on them.
Catching the Mule risks the disguise more than any empty-dock window.
options.consequence: You take the richest version of the prize, and the highest exposure with it. The caisson goes with the Mule inside, and the Combine loses its dock and a DropShip together. But a flooded ship full of survivors is a flooded ship full of people asking how, and you need them to reach 'bad luck', not 'sabotage'.

costs.resource: the disguise's margin, spent to catch a hull in the basin among its own crew and witnesses
costs.risk: a trapped ship's survivors are the most motivated investigators of an 'accident' you could hand them

options.title: When the Dock Is Empty
advantages: Wait for an empty basin and a minimal crew. This is the cleanest, least-witnessed caisson failure available.
It gives the best chance the Combine writes it off as structural and repairs in place.
It is the safest extraction for the demolition team.
disadvantages: An empty dock gives up the trapped-ship bonus, so you get the dock and nothing more.
Waiting for the right window costs time, and the charges sit in place risking discovery.
An empty-dock failure is the least damaging version: the Combine loses a building, not a fleet.
options.consequence: You take the surest, quietest win and let the fleet sail another day. The caisson fails to an empty basin, the Combine's engineers shrug and start a repair estimate, and the band grounds slowly over the season as deferred maintenance does the work you chose not to do all at once.

costs.resource: the days the placed charges sit waiting for an empty-dock window, at risk of discovery the whole time
costs.risk: waiting for the clean window means days of placed demolition sitting one inspection away from being found

options.title: On a Storm
advantages: Time the failure to a coastal storm. Heavy weather is the most natural cause a caisson could have, and the best cover for an approach and exit.
The disguise almost writes itself, because everyone knows storms break docks.
The weather grounds the Combine's own watch and air assets.
disadvantages: You are at the mercy of the weather's schedule, not your own, and a storm may not come inside the operational window.
Working a caisson in heavy seas is deadly for the demolition team.
A storm that breaks the dock also endangers the team's own extraction.
options.consequence: You let the planet provide the alibi and strike under the storm that explains everything. If the weather cooperates, the caisson fails to the sea and not a soul suspects a hand in it. If you must wait for a storm that never comes, the charges age in place and the window runs out around them.

costs.resource: the operation's timing surrendered to the weather, plus a demolition worked in heavy seas
costs.risk: a storm keeps no schedule but its own: wait for it and the window closes, work in it and the sea is an enemy too

entries.event: The team is in position at the caisson, by sea, by yard pass, or under cover of the diversion. The charges are placed or going in. The disguise is intact, and the clock to discovery has started.
A Combine guard round or yard-crew movement passes near the gate. The team holds, hides, or bluffs. A single bad contact here can unmask the whole operation before the charges blow.
Charges are set and the timing is chosen. The team begins extraction, or holds for its window: empty dock, occupied basin, or storm. Every extra minute on site raises the risk of discovery.
The caisson goes. The basin floods and the gate fails. If the disguise held, it reads as a structural collapse. If a shot was fired or a saboteur was seen, the Combine already knows better.
The port mobilizes to the flooded dock. Whether the Combine is responding to an accident or hunting an attacker depends entirely on what your unit left behind.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The limit here is discovery, not a clock. The operation succeeds the moment the caisson fails believably. It fails the moment a Combine hand sees a charge, a swimmer, or a muzzle flash. Drop the gate clean and the Hable Combine spends its season repairing a dock it thinks broke on its own, while its ships ground one by one for want of it. Drop it dirty, meaning seen or shot or obviously sabotaged, and the Combine repairs nothing. It relocates, it retaliates, and it hunts the unit that just started a war {EMPLOYER} paid to avoid.

opforSketch.composition: The Hable Combine's port garrison: a security detail of {GARRISON_STRENGTH} (Regular, light weapons and patrol vehicles), a civilian-pressed yard crew (non-combatant but numerous and observant), and a reaction element of 2-3 salvage 'Mechs and technicals (Regular) that can respond to the dock but is not expecting an attack. The Combine's armed Mule sits in the basin under overhaul, its weapons cold but its crew aboard. Generator should keep this mission's contact light and avoidance-driven — the operation is sabotage, not battle — and field the reaction 'Mechs only if the disguise breaks and the raid goes loud.
opforSketch.behavior: The Combine guards the port like an owner, not a soldier: routine patrols, lax in the way long-unchallenged garrisons become, alert mainly to theft and intrusion rather than demolition. They are not braced for a covert strike on the dock itself, which is the operation's whole opening. But a Combine that realizes it was attacked responds with a wronged owner's fury — fast, thorough, and personal — because the dock is the source of everything the band is, and an attack on it is an attack on the band's future.

forks.name: OPERATION LOW TIDE
forks.trigger: The caisson is destroyed, the wreck reads as an accident, and a Combine hull was caught in the basin.
forks.consequence: The Hable Combine grounds over the season exactly as {EMPLOYER} intended, and it blames its own bad luck. With the band's ships stuck planetside and unmaintained, {EMPLOYER} funds the follow-on the whole sabotage was setting up. It is a strike on a Combine that can no longer get off the ground to run or to fight.

forks.name: OPERATION HIGH WATER
forks.trigger: The sabotage is discovered, or the caisson survives.
forks.consequence: The Combine knows it was attacked and reacts the way {EMPLOYER} paid to prevent. It relocates what hulls it can, hunts the saboteurs, and comes for {EMPLOYER}'s interests in the region. Your follow-on is a running fight against an enraged band that now knows your face and is repairing its dock out of spite.

forks.name: OPERATION SLACK BASIN
forks.trigger: The dock is wrecked but the disguise is ambiguous, or the caisson is only partly collapsed.
forks.consequence: The Combine half-suspects sabotage and half-blames the structure, and the dock is damaged but salvageable with effort. The follow-on is a second strike to finish the caisson before the Combine's engineers can shore it up, this time against a port that is watching the gate.

storyElementSeed: On the caisson's seaward face, a swimmer works a charge into a structural seam by feel in the dark water. She pauses with one hand flat on the cold steel. This gate was built before the Blackout to outlast everyone now alive. The last thing it will ever do is exactly what this stranger's hands tell it to.

STORM_WINDOW_DAYS.unit: days to the next storm window

resourceGates.lackingText: No coastal staging site: the seaborne approach launches from a hired fishing boat whose owner must be paid for his silence as well as his hull — add 7,000 C-bills and a witness who saw divers go over the side the night the dock 'failed'.

Insufficient funds to mount a convincing diversion: the nuisance raid shrinks to a token probe that pulls only part of the security detail — leave a heavier watch on the dock than the gate team needs, and a Combine less convinced the noise was the real event.

title: OPERATION SALT MARCH
skeleton: an interdiction element must intercept a raider convoy hauling captured skilled workers across open desert at night and free them before it reaches the band's fortified base, where the prize is the people not the wreckage and the convoy will scatter or kill the captives at the first sign of attack, so the crux is taking a moving column without triggering the slaughter the attack itself invites
inspiration: WWII liberation of a moving prisoner column; the long forced marches of skilled-labor captives
situation:
The Dark Age has made skilled people scarcer than 'Mechs. The band that calls itself the Sere has noticed. They no longer raid for machines. They raid for the people who build and fix them. Three weeks ago the Sere hit a string of {WORLD} industrial settlements and took {CAPTIVE_COUNT} people. These are fabrication techs, reactor hands, and medical staff — the skilled workers a frontier world cannot easily replace. The band wants them to run its own shops, or to sell to the highest bidder. {EMPLOYER} speaks for the settlements these people were taken from. Your contact there is {NPC:employer-contact}, and the contract is plain: get them back.

The captives are no longer in one place. {NPC:intel-source} reports the Sere is moving them overland to its fortified base deep in the desert. They travel in a convoy of trucks with a light 'Mech escort, moving by night to dodge the heat and any watching eyes. A herder saw the convoy and counted the trucks, and gave a rough route. That sighting is four days old, so treat it as likely but not certain. Once the column reaches the base, the people disappear behind walls no raiding party can breach. So this is a field rescue now and would become a siege later. {EMPLOYER} is paying you to win it in the field, before the walls close around them.

The hard ground is the salt flats. The convoy's route crosses {ROUTE_KM} kilometers of open desert and dry salt pan between the settlements and the base. There is no cover out there and the sightlines run to the horizon. The column will see you coming from far off, and you will be just as exposed to it. The flats are also the only ground a truck convoy can cross, since no other road exists. That makes them the one place the rescue can happen, and the worst place to try it.

Here is what turns this from a battle into a rescue. The captives are the band's cargo and its leverage. A convoy under attack will scatter its trucks across the flats. Worse, its guards may decide dead prisoners are safer than freed ones. You can guess the guards' orders: scatter at the first real attack, and if scattering fails, make sure the captives never arrive anywhere. So you must stop a moving column in the open without giving those guards the moment, or the reason, to kill {CAPTIVE_COUNT} skilled people to send a message.

objectives.primary: Free the captured workers from the Sere convoy and get them out alive. Reach them before the column arrives at the band's fortified base. The people are the prize, not the convoy.
objectives.secondary: Take the column without triggering a massacre. Deny the guards any moment to scatter or kill the captives. A clumsy assault will lose the very people you came to save.
objectives.bonus: Capture the escort 'Mechs and trucks too. The trucks give the freed workers transport, and the loss hurts the Sere's ability to raid again.

complications.name: The Cargo Is the Prize
complications.text: The captives are the whole point of this job. They are unarmed, exhausted, and riding in the trucks you have to attack. Every shot at the convoy lands near the people you were hired to save.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Captives you kill with your own fire count against the primary objective. The more you hurt, the worse you score. You cannot shoot the trucks freely, because the captives are inside them. Only the escort 'Mechs and guard vehicles are safe to hit, and those stay close to the trucks on purpose to make targeting hard.

complications.name: The Scatter Order
complications.text: At the first sign of a serious attack, the Sere's guards will scatter the trucks across the flats. And if they get cornered, a raider band's cold logic takes over: dead prisoners cannot be rescued.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A serious attack that the guards notice triggers a scatter-or-kill response. To take the column you need one of two things. Either move fast enough to seize the trucks before the order goes out, or use an approach that does not look like a serious attack until it is too late to scatter. A slow, obvious assault turns the prize into casualties.

complications.name: The Open Flats
complications.text: There is no cover for kilometers, and the sightlines run all the way out. The convoy will see you coming. The moment it does, you are committed across open ground.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The terrain hides nothing on the way in. Your surprise has to come from timing, darkness, or deception, not from cover. Once the fight starts, both sides stand in the open with no defensive ground. If the rescue bogs down, whatever the base sends out will catch you there.

decisionPoints.name: How to Take the Column
decisionPoints.context: A convoy moving across open flats at night. Its guards will scatter or kill the cargo the instant they read a real attack. You decide how to stop the column without triggering the response that destroys the prize.

options.title: Block and Overrun
advantages: Get ahead of the column, block the road, and overrun the escort fast, seizing the trucks before the scatter order can be given
A column halted and swarmed in seconds has no time to break apart
Decisive if your timing is perfect and you take the escort in the first rush
disadvantages: A block the convoy sees coming gives the guards the exact warning that triggers a scatter
The escort hugs the trucks, so overrunning it means fighting meters from the captives
If the rush stalls, the column scatters across the flats and the rescue becomes a roundup under fire
options.consequence: You bet you can move faster than a guard's trigger finger. A clean block-and-overrun takes the whole column intact before a single truck breaks away. But if the guards spot the block too early, or your rush bogs down, the Sere gets the seconds it needs. It turns the cargo into casualties and scatters the rest into the dark.

costs.resource: everything rides on beating the scatter order in the open, with no second try if the rush stalls
costs.risk: a block the convoy sees coming is the warning that scatters or kills the prize

options.title: Pose as the Reception
advantages: Meet the convoy on the road disguised as the band's own people, such as a relief escort or a guide sent to bring them in, and slip inside the column before a shot is fired
The only approach that puts you among the trucks with the guards off their guard
You secure the captives from within before the escort knows it is under attack
disadvantages: The disguise has to survive close inspection, and the Sere's guards know their own people
A team small enough to pass as a reception party is small against the full escort if the cover breaks
The worst case is being exposed mid-column, stuck among the trucks when the scatter order goes
options.consequence: You walk into the column wearing the enemy's face and take it from the inside. If the disguise holds, you have your hands on the trucks before the guards can reach for their orders. If it breaks, you are in a close fight in the middle of the convoy, with the captives caught between you and your own supporting force.

costs.resource: a disguise that must fool guards who know their own outriders, with one chance to pass the check
costs.risk: a disguise blown mid-column puts you among the trucks at the exact moment the scatter order lands

options.title: Cut the Escort From the Cargo
advantages: Hit the escort 'Mechs and draw them away from the trucks with a feint, then send a second team to seize the now-unguarded convoy
Separates the targets you can shoot from the prize you cannot
Keeps the heavy fighting away from the captives
disadvantages: The escort may ignore the bait and close on the trucks instead, since guards told to protect the cargo do not give chase
Splitting your force between the feint and the seizure weakens both halves
If the feint fails to pull the escort, the seizure team faces the full guard right on top of the trucks
options.consequence: You try to peel the wolves off the flock before you reach for it. If the escort takes the bait, you seize the trucks clean while the 'Mechs chase a ghost. If the guards keep their discipline and stay on the cargo, you have split your force for nothing, and the seizure team meets the whole escort at the trucks.

costs.resource: your force split between a feint and a seizure, betting the escort can be lured off its cargo
costs.risk: a disciplined escort ignores the bait and the seizure team hits the full guard alone

decisionPoints.name: Getting Them Clear
decisionPoints.context: The column is taken and {CAPTIVE_COUNT} exhausted people are free on the open flats. The band's base lies somewhere ahead, and it will send out whatever it has the moment the convoy fails to arrive. You decide how to move the freed workers off the flats before the desert and the Sere close in.

options.title: Lift Them Out
advantages: Bring a DropShip down onto the flats and load the freed workers straight aboard, the fastest way off open ground and clear of the base's reaction
Gets the captives out before the Sere can step in
The open flats at least make good landing ground
disadvantages: A DropShip on the flats is visible to the horizon and to the base, so it announces the rescue and may pull the reaction onto the landing zone
Loading {CAPTIVE_COUNT} exhausted people takes time the band's response may not give you
If the lift is contested, the captives are stuck in the open at the landing zone during the worst of it
options.consequence: You reach for the sky and trust speed to beat the base's response. A clean lift gets the captives off-world before the Sere can form a pursuit. A contested one turns the landing zone into the battle, with the freed workers loading under the very guns the rescue was meant to outrun.

costs.resource: a DropShip tied to an exposed desert landing zone, visible to the base and slow to load a crowd
costs.risk: a contested lift fights the band's reaction with the captives in the open on the ramp

options.title: Drive Them Out Overland
advantages: Use the convoy's own captured trucks to drive the freed workers off the flats by a route the base does not expect, quiet and with no aircraft or landing zone to give the rescue away
The band may not realize the convoy is lost until it is long overdue, which buys you a head start
Keeps the trucks the bonus objective wants and keeps the captives moving
disadvantages: A ground withdrawal across the flats is slow and exposed until you reach cover
Captured trucks are easy to recognize, so the band's own aircraft or outriders may spot them
A long overland run gives the base's reaction a long time to find and catch a column of exhausted people
options.consequence: You drive the prize out the way it came in, on the enemy's own wheels. A clean overland exit slips the captives away before the Sere knows to look. A discovered one becomes a running chase across open ground, with a truckload of exhausted civilians and the band's fast units closing from behind.

costs.resource: a slow overland withdrawal in easily recognized captured trucks across ground with no cover
costs.risk: a long run across the open gives the base's pursuit a long window to overtake a column of exhausted people

options.title: Go to Ground and Wait
advantages: Move the freed workers to the nearest broken ground or settlement and lie low while the Sere's reaction sweeps the flats and wears itself out
Avoids the running fight that a hot extraction invites
Lets the band tire itself out searching open ground while the captives sit safely off it
disadvantages: {CAPTIVE_COUNT} exhausted people need water, shelter, and medical care that you must provide while hiding them
If a search finds the hide, you fight with civilians underfoot and no way out
Waiting hands the time and the initiative to the band
options.consequence: You trade speed for patience and hide the prize until the storm passes. Done well, the Sere wears itself out searching empty flats while the captives recover under cover. Done poorly, the band runs you to ground with the people you saved, trapped in a hide with no way out and an enemy that has finally found what it lost.

costs.resource: shelter, water, and medical care for a crowd of exhausted people while hiding from an active search
costs.risk: a hide that is discovered becomes a last stand with civilians underfoot and no way off the flats

entries.event: Contact. You reach the convoy on the flats by block, disguise, or feint, and the rescue begins. How the Sere escort first reads the situation decides whether the scatter order goes out.

The scatter decision. If the guards judge this a serious attack, the trucks break formation and the worst orders are given. If your approach caught them by surprise, you engage the escort before it can scatter the cargo.
The column is secured or scattering. The freed captives are exhausted, frightened, and some are hurt, and you must gather and move them. The band's base, now overdue a convoy, will soon notice.
The base reaction window opens. With the convoy past due, the Sere base sends outriders or a relief 'Mech unit toward the route to find out why.
The base reaction reaches the flats. Any rescue still on the open ground with its captives is now in a fight against the band's home guard, with civilians in the middle of it.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: You must take the convoy and get the captives moving before the base reacts to a column that never arrived. That window opens around T+2:00 and slams shut by T+5:00, when the Sere's home guard reaches the flats. Free the workers and get them off the open ground inside that window, and {EMPLOYER}'s people come home. Bog down on the flats, or give the escort a moment to scatter and kill, and the rescue turns into a battle fought over the bodies of the people you came to save, against a band fighting for its stolen future on ground that hides no one.

opforSketch.composition: The Sere convoy escort: a guard force of {ESCORT_STRENGTH} (Regular, mounted in the trucks and technicals) plus a light 'Mech escort of 2-4 salvage machines (Regular) that travels close to the cargo by design. The band's base, offscreen until it reacts, can dispatch a reaction element of 'Mechs and technicals (Regular, Veteran command) to the route. The captives are non-combatant cargo. Generator should keep the escort's 'Mechs and vehicles as the engageable force, treat the captive trucks as no-fire objectives, and field the base reaction as a separate, later OPFOR group on the campaign clock.
opforSketch.behavior: The Sere escort guards cargo, not ground: it keeps its 'Mechs tight to the trucks, refuses bait that would pull it off the convoy, and follows a brutal standing logic — disperse under serious attack, and deny the enemy the prize by any means if dispersal fails. They are not fanatics; they are raiders protecting an investment, and they will run rather than die for it once the cargo is clearly lost. The base reaction, when it comes, fights harder — it is defending the band's home and its future labor pool both.

forks.name: OPERATION HOMECOMING
forks.trigger: The captives are freed and brought out alive, and the convoy's transport and escort are taken.
forks.consequence: The settlements get their skilled people back. {EMPLOYER} keeps you on to guard the recovering industrial towns against the Sere's certain return. Better still, the freed techs have seen the band's base from the inside, and they can tell you exactly where the next blow should fall.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY TRUCKS
forks.trigger: The captives are scattered or killed, or the column reaches the base.
forks.consequence: The rescue fails on the flats, or arrives too late, and the captives are dead, scattered, or behind the Sere's walls. Now {EMPLOYER} faces the siege problem the field rescue was meant to avoid: a strike on the fortified base itself, to free whoever of the {CAPTIVE_COUNT} is still alive.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WALK
forks.trigger: Some captives are freed, but you are forced to go to ground with them under active pursuit.
forks.consequence: You have the people but not a way out. The band's home guard is quartering the flats, and you have a column of exhausted civilians to move through it. What follows is a fighting retreat across the desert to a working extraction point, set to the pace of the captives and hunted by a band that will not stop looking for what was taken from it.

storyElementSeed: In a halted truck on the salt pan, a fabrication tech who has not slept in three days watches your machines through a tear in the canvas. She does the only arithmetic she has left. How many guards, how many of these strangers, how far to the dark edge of the flats. Then, without being told, she decides which of the others she will carry if it comes to running.

resourceGates.lackingText: No owned DropShip for a desert pickup: the lift runs on a chartered lander on a fixed schedule the unit cannot move — add 10,000 C-bills and accept that the rescue's timing is now the charter pilot's timing, not the band's and not the unit's.

No prepared hide or friendly settlement in reach: the captives must shelter in improvised desert cover with field stores only — add 6,000 C-bills in water and medical supplies and a far higher chance the band's search finds the hide before it gives up.

title: OPERATION QUIET WATCH
skeleton: a counter-reconnaissance screen must locate and destroy a pirate pathfinder team mapping a defended world's approaches for a coming raid fleet, where the scouts move only in sensor-dead terrain and the screen must let them survey enough to be found, then kill them before they transmit, so the crux is hunting the enemy's eyes and silencing them before they report rather than meeting the raid itself
inspiration: counter-reconnaissance screening; the hunt for enemy scouting and weather-reporting parties before a major operation
situation:
Before a raider fleet attacks a world, it sends scouts to map it first. {WORLD} now knows it has scouts on it. {WORLD} is worth mapping because of its industry. It has foundries and fabrication plants — fixed wealth that a large raider coalition would cross jumps to strip. For two weeks {NPC:intel-source} has been gathering signs of a scout team at work. Someone disturbed the ground near the approach corridors. A hunter found a cold camp. A fisherman reported a light aircraft where no aircraft should fly. This is patient, professional scouting, not a casual smash-and-grab. The signs are between 3 and 14 days old, so the read is fairly confident but not certain. Someone is mapping {WORLD}'s defenses, its approach lanes, and its landing grounds. When the map is done, it goes to whoever is assembling the fleet.

{EMPLOYER} runs {WORLD}'s industry, and its contact {NPC:employer-contact} has hired your unit. You are not here to fight the raid. You are here to blind it. Find the scout team and destroy it before it can transmit its map. If the fleet never gets the map, the world stops being worth the trip. Kill the scouts and the raid loses its eyes. Let them report and {WORLD} faces an attack planned in detail against defenses the enemy already knows cold.

The hard part is the terrain, because it defeats sensors. The scouts work the {DISTRICT} highlands. It is a maze of deep ravines, mineral-heavy ridges that blind sensors, and low ground you cannot see into. A small, careful team can move and camp there unseen. A 'Mech can rule the open valleys, but the scouts never enter them. The survey happens in the folds and shadows, where your own sensors are as blind as everyone else's. Finding the team means hunting it through ground chosen to defeat the hunt.

This is a patience game, not a simple manhunt. The scouts are not finished yet. A team that knows it is hunted will hide and wait you out, or send an early, incomplete report. So your problem is doubled. You must let the scouts keep working long enough to track them by where they survey. At the same time, you must be ready to kill them before they transmit. Hunt too hard and they vanish. Hunt too soft and they finish and report. The survey you must stop is the same survey that, watched closely, shows you where the scouts are.

objectives.primary: Find and destroy the pirate scout team before it sends its map of {WORLD}'s defenses to the raid fleet gathering beyond the jump points.
objectives.secondary: Stop any partial transmission. A scout team that knows it is found will try to send what it has. Even an incomplete map gives the fleet enough to plan from. Kill the team before the signal goes out, not after.
objectives.bonus: Recover the team's map data and identify the fleet behind it. This turns the enemy's own scouting into {WORLD}'s warning of who is coming and when. The raid can then be met or stopped early, not just delayed.

complications.name: The Sensor-Dead Ground
complications.text: The scouts work the one kind of ground that beats sensors. Mineral ridges, deep ravines, and blind low ground. They chose it so a defender's usual tools cannot find a small team.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You cannot find the scouts with a sensor sweep or a 'Mech patrol of the open ground, because they never use it. Finding them takes reading the pattern of their survey work, sending observers on foot into the blind ground, or guessing where they must go next. This is slow, on-foot, intelligence-led work, not a sensor net.

complications.name: Hunt Too Hard, They Vanish
complications.text: A scout team's first skill is knowing when it is hunted. Press the search and the scouts hide and wait you out, or send what they have and disappear. Either way you lose.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Open, heavy searching raises how aware the scouts are that they are being hunted. If that awareness gets high, the team goes still. The survey pauses, and your chance to track them by their activity closes. Or they send an early report and slip away. The hunt must stay quiet enough to let the scouts keep working while you close on them.

complications.name: The Transmission
complications.text: The map is worthless to the fleet until it is sent, and it can be sent in minutes. The whole operation comes down to reaching the team before the signal leaves. A kill one second after the transmission is a kill that saved nothing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The scouts carry the gear to transmit and will use it the instant they are in real danger. Your strike must land before the transmission starts, or at the same moment. A strike that warns the team without instantly killing its comms lets the map get out. Finding their transmitter is itself one way to find the team.

decisionPoints.name: How to Find the Scouts
decisionPoints.context: The scout team is working ground that is built to hide it. You must both stop its survey and use that survey to find it. Decide how to hunt scouts who are watching for hunters. Remember that the search itself can scare them into hiding or into transmitting early.

options.title: Read the Survey Pattern
advantages: Map where the scouts have already surveyed, then work out where they must go next
Meet them at the approach corridor or landing ground they have not covered yet
This is the quietest method, with no visible search and no warning to the team
Getting ahead of the scouts is better than chasing behind them
disadvantages: This needs the survey signs {NPC:intel-source} is still collecting, so it is slow and stays incomplete until enough points are plotted
A team that varies its routine or surveys out of order breaks the pattern
Guess wrong and you wait at an empty ridge while the scouts finish somewhere else
options.consequence: You hunt by getting inside the scouts' own plan. You meet them where they must go, not where they have already been. Read it right and the team walks into a waiting kill before it knows it was found. Read it wrong and you sit in ambush at the wrong ravine while the survey finishes a valley over.

costs.resource: 7 days of patient sign-gathering before the pattern is solid enough to act on
costs.risk: a scout team that surveys out of order leaves your ambush waiting at an empty ridge

options.title: Flood the Dead Ground With Eyes
advantages: Fill the highlands with observers on foot, hunters, and small sensor posts so the scouts cannot avoid every watcher
Enough watchers will eventually catch a careful team in someone's line of sight
More eyes also catch a transmission the moment it starts
disadvantages: A highland full of your observers is activity the scouts will notice, so their awareness of the hunt climbs fast
Watch posts on foot are exposed if the scouts decide to fight their way clear
This is slow to set up and ties down your people across rough country
options.consequence: You fill the scouts' hiding ground with watchers and trust numbers to find what stealth hides. Do it quietly enough and a watcher catches the team in the open between hides. Do it too heavily and the scouts feel the country fill up around them. Then they go to ground or transmit before a single observer gets a clean look.

costs.resource: your people spread thin as watch posts across the highlands, thin everywhere so they can be present anywhere
costs.risk: a highland visibly full of watchers warns the scouts and tips them into hiding or transmitting early

options.title: Bait the Map
advantages: Fake a weak spot in {WORLD}'s defenses, such as an unguarded approach corridor, too tempting for a scout to skip
Wait for the team to come and confirm it, which pulls them to a place and time you choose
A team focused on checking the bait has its guard turned the wrong way
disadvantages: A fake gap that looks like a trap tells the scouts the defender knows it is being watched, and a weakness that is too obvious is itself a warning
If the team checks the bait from very far off, you may spot them but not reach them before they move on
If the kill fails, the scouts may record your fake gap as real intelligence
options.consequence: You write a lie into your own defenses to pull the enemy's eyes to one spot. A clean bait brings the scouts into a kill zone you built. A clumsy one warns the scouts that {WORLD} knows it is being mapped. And a failed kill leaves them alive with your fake gap recorded as fact in their map.

costs.resource: a fake weak spot in {WORLD}'s defenses that the scouts may record as real if the kill misses
costs.risk: a bait read as a trap warns the scouts the defender is hunting them

decisionPoints.name: The Kill
decisionPoints.context: You have found the scout team. It carries the map and the gear to send it. It will transmit the instant it knows it is in real danger. Decide how to take the team before the signal leaves.

options.title: Silent Overwhelm
advantages: Hit the team with a fast, close, silent assault by specialists on foot, with no warning
Knock out their comms in the first seconds, before a transmission can start
This is the only method that reliably beats the signal, because the team dies before it knows it is found
You recover the map intact for the bonus
disadvantages: You must get a strike team onto the scouts unseen in their own chosen ground, which is the hardest approach of all
A team warned even a moment early sends the transmission as it dies
There is no 'Mech support in the blind ground where the kill must happen
options.consequence: You kill the scouts with a hand over the mouth, close and quiet and final before the signal can leave. Do it perfectly and the map never goes out. It falls into your hands instead. Do it a second too slow and the team's last act is the transmission that makes the whole operation pointless.

costs.resource: a strike team on foot committed to a silent close kill in the scouts' own sensor-dead ground
costs.risk: a team warned one second early sends the map with its dying breath

options.title: Jam, Then Strike
advantages: Blanket the team's area with radio jamming the instant before the assault, so even if the scouts try to transmit, the signal does not get out
This gives the strike room for error, because the team can know it is hit and still fail to report
It lets you use a heavier, faster assault without needing perfect silence
disadvantages: Jamming is itself a signal, so the moment it starts the scouts know they are found and being silenced
A determined team may have a tough or tightly aimed radio link that the jamming misses
Jamming works poorly over sensor-dead terrain, the same ground that hides the team
options.consequence: You slam the door on the signal, then break the door down. The jamming keeps the map from leaving even if the strike is loud. The exception is a team with a link that punches through, in which case the jamming only told them to send while they still could.

costs.resource: electronic-warfare jamming gear committed to a blanket over the same terrain that defeats sensors
costs.risk: jamming announces the kill and may miss a tough radio link the team kept in reserve

options.title: Take One Alive
advantages: Strike to capture rather than kill, because a live scout is the map, the fleet's identity, and the raid's timing in one prisoner
This turns the bonus from data recovery into a full intelligence haul on who is coming and when
A captured scout can be made to reveal what the map alone would not
disadvantages: Capture is harder and slower than a kill, and the extra seconds are exactly the seconds a transmission needs
A team taken alive but allowed to send first has cost you everything for one prisoner
Scouts may be equipped or ordered to destroy their data and themselves rather than be taken
options.consequence: You reach for the whole prize, not just to blind the fleet but to unmask it. A clean capture hands {WORLD} the enemy's plan from the enemy's own mouth. But a capture that lets the transmission slip, or that finds the scouts have wiped their data and died rather than talk, leaves you a corpse and an empty datacore, and it cost you the speed a clean kill would have had.

costs.resource: the speed of the kill, slowed to take a prisoner who may transmit or self-destruct in the extra seconds
costs.risk: a capture attempt gives the transmission the seconds a kill would have denied it

entries.event: The team is found, by pattern, by watch post, or at the bait, and the strike begins. From this instant it is a race between your assault and how fast the scouts can transmit.
The scouts react. The moment they sense real danger, they reach for the transmitter. Your attack on their comms must already be underway, not just starting.

This is the transmission window. If the team's comms are not down by now, the map goes out, whole or in part, to the fleet beyond the jump points. After this, the kill saves nothing the enemy does not already have.
The team is dead or has escaped. Take them before they transmit and the map and the fleet's identity are yours. If they sent first, {WORLD} is now a mapped target.

The fleet responds. Silence from its scouts eventually tells it that its eyes are gone. Whether it drops {WORLD} as too costly to map blind, or comes anyway on what it has, depends on whether anything was sent.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The deadline is the transmission, measured in seconds, not days. The map is worthless to the fleet until it is sent, and it decides everything the instant it is. Find the scouts and silence them before the signal leaves, and the raid fleet loses the map that made the trip worth taking. Let them send, whole or in part, and {WORLD}'s defenses, approaches, and landing grounds are an open book for whoever is assembling the ships beyond the jump points. The next force across the dead ground will not be a scout team.

opforSketch.composition: The pirate pathfinder team: a small, elite reconnaissance element — {SCOUT_STRENGTH} specialists (Veteran/Elite), dismounted or in a single light aircraft and a stealthed light 'Mech or fast vehicle, equipped for survey and long-range transmission, not for battle. They avoid contact by doctrine. Behind them, offscreen, the assembling raid coalition — a fleet-scale threat the survey would enable, which appears on the campaign layer only as the consequence of success or failure here. Generator should keep this mission's contact small-scale and stealth-driven; the pathfinders fight only to break contact and transmit, and the real enemy is the raid this recon prevents.
opforSketch.behavior: The pathfinders are professionals at not being found: they move only in sensor-dead ground, camp cold, vary their routine, and watch constantly for the defender's reaction. They will not fight for ground or pride — their entire mission is to survey and report, and a threatened team's reflex is to transmit and vanish, not to stand. Their one predictable behavior is the survey itself, which must cover certain ground to be useful, and which is therefore the thread by which a patient hunter can find them before they finish.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR SKY
forks.trigger: The scouts are destroyed before transmission, and their map and the fleet's identity are recovered.
forks.consequence: The raid fleet is blind, and {WORLD} knows who was coming. {EMPLOYER} keeps your unit on to ready the world against a coalition that may still come on guesswork. Or you carry the recovered intelligence to whoever can hit the fleet at its assembly point before it ever sails.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN BOOK
forks.trigger: The map is transmitted, in whole or in part, to the fleet.
forks.consequence: {WORLD}'s defenses are now mapped, and the raid coalition holds the map. The attack the scouts were preparing comes planned in detail against known ground. Your next job is to defend a world whose every weakness the enemy already holds on a datacore. It is the raid the operation was meant to prevent, and now it arrives warned.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND TEAM
forks.trigger: The scout team is destroyed but turns out to be one of two, and the second is still at large.
forks.consequence: The survey is stopped but not ended. A second scout team is working another quarter of {WORLD}. The fleet will have half its map and reason to wonder about the rest. Your next job is the same hunt again, against a team now warned by its partner's silence that {WORLD} kills scouts.

storyElementSeed: High in the mineral ridges, one of your observers has lain still under a dust-colored tarp for six hours. Then she sees it. Not a man, but a shadow that is wrong — it has moved since morning. It is a camouflage net, set by someone good enough to be worth killing, and set just a little too well for the ground it sits on.

SURVEY_DAYS_LEFT.unit: days until the survey is complete

resourceGates.appliesTo: Flood the Dead Ground With Eyes
resourceGates.lackingText: No local base to run a picket screen from: the observers must be hired from {WORLD}'s hunters and herders, untrained and talkative — add 7,000 C-bills and accept that a picket line of locals is a picket line the scouts may hear about before they see it.

No EW budget: jamming runs on improvised, under-powered emitters that cover only part of the band and only briefly — narrow the jamming window and accept a real chance the survey slips through the gaps in it.

title: OPERATION SCATTERED COIN
skeleton: an interdiction element must hit a raider band's season of looted tribute as it moves overland to a buyer's pickup, where the haul is deliberately split into many small dispersed columns on different routes so no one ambush takes it all, forcing a choice between the richest column and the one carrying the band's leadership and ledger, so the crux is which dispersed serial to take when the unit can catch only one or two
inspiration: interdiction of dispersed caravan traffic; T. E. Lawrence's raids on scattered Hejaz traffic, 1917-18
situation:
Once a year, the raider band called the Tasker Run cashes out. A whole season of loot — salvaged 'Mech parts, refined metal, hijacked cargo, the plunder of a dozen raids — moves overland to a buyer. There an off-world fence trades it for hard cash and clean credit. {EMPLOYER}, through {NPC:employer-contact}, wants that handoff hit. Rob the robbers, cost the Tasker Run its payday, and bring back the loot, the leaders, or both. This comes from a former band teamster who sold the routes, so the picture is six days old and only fairly reliable.

The band has been robbed before and learned. The loot does not travel as one fat convoy you can ambush whole.
