It moves as {COLUMN_COUNT} small columns — a few vehicles each, spread over several days on different roads through the {DISTRICT} hill country. That way no single ambush can take more than a slice. The band expects to lose one column; it has made sure nobody can take them all. The columns are not equal. {NPC:intel-source} thinks one carries the richest single share, and another carries the band's leaders and their ledger — the record of buyers, hidden caches, and debts, worth more to {EMPLOYER} than the loot itself. Which column is which is a best guess, not a fact.

The ground is the second problem. The hill country is a maze of ridgelines, wooded draws, and narrow valley roads. The columns thread through it on separate routes. You can catch a column at a chokepoint, but you cannot sit in two valleys at once. The same broken ground that lets the band scatter also gives you good ambush sites — but every column you cover is one you leave open, and the routes are far enough apart that catching two means splitting a force barely strong enough to be sure of one.

Here is the trap. Every column is racing the same {TRANSFER_WINDOW}-day clock to the buyer, and once a column arrives its share is paid for and gone. You cannot watch every road or catch every column, and you must pick your target before you can confirm what it carries: the richest haul, the leaders and ledger, or a gamble on catching two and being sure of neither. The band has turned your strength against you — one good ambush is not enough when the prize was built to be caught only in pieces.

objectives.primary: Hit the Tasker Run's loot movement. Take the haul, the leaders and ledger, or both, before the columns reach the buyer and the season's plunder turns into the band's spending money.
objectives.secondary: Cost the band its payday even where you cannot carry the loot off. A column wrecked or scattered before it reaches the buyer is plunder the Tasker Run never gets paid for.
objectives.bonus: Capture the band's ledger intact. It lists their buyers, caches, and debts, and it turns one ambush into a map of the whole network for the missions that follow.

complications.name: Split So You Can't Take It All
complications.text: The loot moves as {COLUMN_COUNT} columns on different roads so no single ambush can take more than a slice. The band has chosen to lose one piece in order to keep the rest.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The prize is spread across several columns you cannot all reach. Catching one column wins one share. Catching two means splitting the force, and a split force can be beaten at both sites. This mission is a choice of which column to take, not one battle to win.

complications.name: Which Column Is Which
complications.text: One column carries the richest haul; another carries the leaders and the ledger. {NPC:intel-source} only has a guess, and the band may have swapped the valuable cargo between columns to beat exactly that guess.
complications.mechanicalEffect: You only know the two high-value columns by shaky intelligence. Commit against the wrong one and you take a small share while the real prize slips past. Confirming what a column carries before you strike costs time the clock may not give you.

complications.name: The Convergence Window
complications.text: Every column is racing the same {TRANSFER_WINDOW}-day clock to the buyer. Once a column arrives, its share is paid for and gone, beyond your reach.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each column that reaches the buyer takes its share out of play. The clock is closing: strike late and fewer columns are still on the road. Any column you let arrive is loot the band cashes, no matter what you do elsewhere.

decisionPoints.name: Which Column to Take
decisionPoints.context: The columns are moving on spread-out routes, and you are strong enough to be sure of one ambush. Intelligence only guesses at which column holds what. You must pick your target before you can confirm what it carries.

options.title: Take the Richest Haul
advantages: Throw your full strength at the column intelligence calls the largest single share — the biggest material prize and the surest payday for {EMPLOYER}
Full strength on one column means a clean, decisive ambush
Loot is loot, whether or not the leaders are in that column
disadvantages: If the guess is wrong, you take a smaller share and the real prize gets away
The richest column may be the most heavily guarded for that very reason
Taking the loot leaves the leaders and ledger free to rebuild and do this again next year
options.consequence: You go for the money with everything you have. Guess right and {EMPLOYER} gets the season's plunder and the band gets a ruinous year. Guess wrong and you fight hard for a slice while the leaders and the richest share both reach the buyer by other roads.

costs.resource: your full strength committed to one column, on a shaky guess about what it carries
costs.risk: a wrong guess wins a small share while the real prize passes through a valley you left open

options.title: Take the Leaders and Ledger
advantages: Strike the column intelligence calls the band's command and records — the prize that breaks the Tasker Run for good, not just for a season
The ledger is the bonus and the key to the whole network
Killing the band's leaders is worth more to a long campaign than any single haul
disadvantages: The leaders' column may be the most alert, the best-guarded, and the most willing to burn its own records rather than hand them over
If the guess is wrong, you spend your strength on middling loot and its guards
Taking the leaders lets most of the season's plunder reach the buyer and fund whatever rises from the wreckage
options.consequence: You go for the head and the books. Guess right and the Tasker Run loses its leaders, its records, and its future in one stroke. Guess wrong and you chase command into the wrong valley while the loot — and maybe the real leaders — slips past to the buyer.

costs.resource: your strength staked on a guess about which column hides the leaders, against a column likely to fight or burn its records
costs.risk: a leaders' column that torches its ledger under attack denies the bonus even in a fight you win

options.title: Split and Take Two
advantages: Divide the force and set up against both high-value columns — refuse the guess and cover the haul and the leaders at once
Removes the risk of betting everything on the wrong column
The only choice that can take the richest haul and the leaders both
disadvantages: A force split in two may be too weak to be sure of either column, and a lone detachment can be wiped out by a strong guard
Two ambushes in separate valleys cannot help each other
Spreading thin is exactly what the band's scattering was built to punish — you risk taking neither prize and losing people at both
options.consequence: You answer their scattering with your own and reach for both prizes at once. If both ambushes hold, the Tasker Run loses its haul and its leaders together. If either detachment meets more than it can handle, you have done the band's work for it — split up, beaten piece by piece, and sure of nothing.

costs.resource: the force divided across two valleys, each detachment alone against whatever guard its column carries
costs.risk: a split force can be beaten piece by piece by the band's strongest guard and take neither prize

decisionPoints.name: How to Hit It
decisionPoints.context: You have picked the target column, and it is threading the hill country toward the buyer. Now decide how to take it — fast and violent, or in a way that keeps the loot whole and the records intact.

options.title: Hard Ambush at a Chokepoint
advantages: Spring a full ambush where the column is boxed in — a draw or a narrow valley road — and destroy or take it before it can react
The surest way to stop a column cold
Broken ground at a chokepoint favors the side that set the trap
disadvantages: A violent ambush risks wrecking the very loot or burning the ledger you came for
Guards under orders may torch the cargo rather than let you capture it
A column that survives the first blow scatters into the hills with its share
options.consequence: You take the column the direct way, with force enough to end the fight fast. A clean chokepoint ambush takes the share intact before the guards can react. A sloppy one wrecks the loot, burns the ledger, or lets a scattered column carry its prize off into ground that hides it.

costs.resource: a violent ambush that risks the very prize it is trying to seize
costs.risk: guards under orders torch the haul or the ledger rather than surrender it

options.title: Block and Demand Surrender
advantages: Block the column with visible, overwhelming force and offer the guards a choice: hand over the cargo and walk — the prize taken intact without a shot
Keeps the haul whole and the ledger unburned
Raider guards paid by the job rarely die for cargo that is not theirs
disadvantages: A column given the choice may use the talk to scatter, signal, or stall until the band's other columns react
Some guards will fight rather than face the leaders having given up the cargo without a fight
A block that lets the column talk is a block that gives the band time
options.consequence: You reach for the prize intact by giving the guards a way out. Most take it and the share is yours, whole and undamaged. A stubborn crew fights anyway, or a clever one talks until it can break for the hills — and your restraint costs you the column you had cornered.

costs.resource: the initiative, handed to guards who may use the talk to scatter or stall
costs.risk: a column allowed to talk buys time to break for cover or signal the band's other columns

options.title: Shadow It to the Buyer
advantages: Do not hit the column on the road at all — follow it to the buyer and take the haul, the leaders, and the fence together where they meet
The richest possible outcome: the whole handoff, buyer included, in one stroke
The buyer's site is where the columns and the band's bosses all come together
disadvantages: Following a column that far means letting it nearly finish its run — if you lose the tail or get spotted, the share is handed over and gone
The buyer's site may be guarded in strength by both the band and the fence's own security
Waiting for the meeting means waiting while other columns arrive and cash out too
options.consequence: You gamble patience for the whole prize, trailing a column to the one place everything comes together. A clean shadow puts the haul, the leaders, and the fence in your hands at once. A blown one leaves you watching the handoff finish from a ridgeline, the share paid for and gone before you can close.

costs.resource: the time and tail discipline to follow a column almost to its destination without being spotted
costs.risk: a tail lost or spotted lets the share change hands at the buyer, gone beyond reach

entries.event: The columns are moving. {COLUMN_COUNT} of them thread the hill country on staggered routes toward the buyer, and the {TRANSFER_WINDOW}-day clock starts counting down.
You commit to your chosen column or columns. From here on, every road you did not cover is a road whose share is running for the buyer unopposed.
The ambush is sprung. The target column is taken, fought, or scattered — and any guard who gets away carries word to the other columns and the band's command that the loot is under attack.
The Tasker Run reacts. Warned columns change routes, speed up toward the buyer, or pull guards in to cover the richest shares. Your chance to catch a second column shrinks fast.
The window closes. Every column that reached the buyer has handed over its share. Whatever you have not taken by now, the band has cashed.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The window closes at T+{TRANSFER_WINDOW} days, when the last columns reach the buyer and the season's plunder turns into the Tasker Run's spending money. Every column you hit before it arrives is loot denied; every column that arrives is paid for and gone. The loot is split across many roads, so one ambush can't catch all of it. You are one ambush. Pick which columns to hit and which to let pass — and you're choosing before you know which one carries the real prize.

opforSketch.composition: The Tasker Run's tribute movement: {COLUMN_COUNT} dispersed columns, each a few cargo vehicles with a light escort of technicals and 1-2 salvage 'Mechs (Regular), staggered over days and routes. The high-value columns — richest haul, leadership and ledger — carry heavier escort (Veteran around the leadership). The buyer's pickup is defended by the band's reserve and the fence's own security (Regular/Veteran) if the unit pushes that far. Generator should field the columns as separate, individually-modest OPFOR groups, with the high-value serials and the pickup as the heavier engagements, and treat the band's strength as real but divided — the dispersion is the defense.
opforSketch.behavior: The Tasker Run protects its season's work by spreading it thin and accepting partial loss: the columns run quietly, avoid contact, and scatter rather than fight to the death for a share. Escorts are paid professionals who will not die for cargo that is not theirs, but the leadership column fights harder and will burn its ledger before surrendering it. Once the movement is known to be under attack, the band consolidates escort onto its most valuable shares and races them to the pickup, trading the lesser columns for the certainty of cashing the greater.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL PURSE
forks.trigger: The haul and the leaders are both taken, or the ledger is recovered intact.
forks.consequence: The Tasker Run loses its season and its secrets together, and the ledger maps the band's buyers, caches, and debts. {EMPLOYER} funds the next step the ledger makes possible: run down the caches and middlemen before the survivors regroup, and turn one ambush into the unraveling of the whole network.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY ROADS
forks.trigger: The chosen columns hold minor shares and the prize reaches the buyer, or the split force is beaten piece by piece.
forks.consequence: You took a slice, or took losses for nothing, while the Tasker Run cashed its season and walked away funded. That payday becomes the war chest for next year's raids. {EMPLOYER}'s next problem is harder and later: a band you were meant to break, now richer than before.

forks.name: OPERATION SHORT COUNT
forks.trigger: The unit takes one valuable column but the other reaches the buyer.
forks.consequence: You have the haul but not the leaders, or the leaders but not the haul — half the prize, and the band hurt but not broken. Now comes the chase for what got away: the share moving off-world, or the leaders who escaped to rebuild on the plunder you let pass.

storyElementSeed: A former band teamster traces the routes on a creased map, naming the valley each column takes. His finger stops over the two that matter, the rich one and the one with the bosses in it. Then, not quite meeting anyone's eyes, he admits the band swaps those two at the last minute, so a map like this one gets a man killed.

resourceGates.lackingText: No forward base to coordinate two separated ambushes: the detachments operate out of contact with each other across the hill country — accept that neither can reinforce the other, and that a detachment in trouble is a detachment alone.

Insufficient funds to sustain a patient shadow operation: the tail runs on minimal supplies and cannot wait out a slow column — shorten the window the unit can follow, raising the chance the shadow is broken off before the pickup.
